mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's FOR possession being well above competition mean (63.4 vs 50.0) AND Team A's FOR shots being well above competition mean (16.7 vs 13.2). Measure corner_kicks FOR Team A in matches where both conditions hold simultaneously, versus matches where only one or neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks FOR Team A rise when both possession dominance and shot volume are jointly elevated, more than when either is elevated alone; the joint condition amplifies corner generation beyond the additive sum of each single-observable effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's dominant possession profile (>63%) combined with its high shot volume (>16 shots/match) jointly predicts a corner-kick generation rate that substantially exceeds what either possession or shots alone would imply, because sustained territorial pressure compounds set-piece opportunities in a non-additive way. The joint condition of high possession AND high shots FOR Team A should be associated with elevated corner-kick totals beyond the baseline corner rate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine two-observable joint relationship (possession AND shots together predicting corners). It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires conditioning on two distinct continuous observables simultaneously and testing whether their joint presence produces a non-additive effect on a third observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each historical match, compute Team A's shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) and pair it against the opponent's shots-on-target allowed rate (shots_on_target AGAINST / shots AGAINST). Condition on the cross-team ratio of these two rates and measure goals FOR Team A. Apply the same logic for Team B attacking against Team A's defensive profile.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals FOR a team rise as the ratio of that team's shots-on-target rate to the opponent's shots-on-target suppression rate increases; the asymmetry between Team A's high on-target rate and Team B's relatively permissive defensive on-target rate should be associated with elevated Team A goal output relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's asymmetric shot-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (FOR: 16.7 shots yielding 6.1 on target) versus Team B's asymmetric ratio (FOR: 11.6 shots yielding 3.9 on target, AGAINST: 12.3 shots allowed yielding 4.5 on target) creates a cross-team asymmetry: Team A's shot quality (on-target rate) against Team B's defensive shot-on-target suppression rate jointly determine goal output in a way that differs from either team's standalone shot or shots-on-target average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a cross-team ratio of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for opposing sides simultaneously — an asymmetric relationship across different observables for the two sides. It is not reducible to one team's shots or shots_on_target alone with a single opponent band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the away team's fouls FOR rate being above competition mean, AND (b) the home team's second-half goals FOR rate exceeding its first-half rate. Measure cards_2h FOR the away team in matches where both conditions hold, versus when only one or neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half cards FOR the away team rise when the away team's foul rate is elevated AND the home team scores more in the second half than the first half; the joint presence of both conditions is associated with more second-half cards than either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation rate (cards_2h FOR: 1.045 per match) combined with its elevated foul rate (fouls FOR: 10.6/match, rising to 10.8 in recent 5) and Team A's high second-half goal-scoring rate (goals FOR 2H: 1.507/match vs 1.067 in 1H) jointly suggest a mechanism where Team B's disciplinary pressure in the second half is associated with Team A's late attacking dominance. The joint condition of Team B committing fouls at an elevated rate AND Team A scoring more in the second half should be associated with higher second-half card totals.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across three observables (fouls, goals by half, cards_2h) and requires within-match half-level resolution for goals. It also involves an asymmetric cross-team conditioning (away team fouls + home team half-split goals). Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks into first-half and second-half totals for both teams. Condition on the cross-team half-level corner differential: (Team A corners FOR 1H minus Team B corners AGAINST 1H) versus (Team A corners FOR 2H minus Team B corners AGAINST 2H). Test whether the half in which Team A's corner advantage is larger predicts the half with more total corners in the match.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The half where Team A's corner generation advantage over Team B's concession rate is larger is associated with a higher share of total match corners occurring in that half; the within-match distribution of corners is non-uniform and predictable from the half-level profiles of both teams jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick generation is strongly split by half (1H: 3.636, 2H: 3.652 FOR; opponent allows 1H: 1.773, 2H: 1.561 AGAINST), while Team B's corner concession rate also differs by half (1H: 2.195, 2H: 2.683 AGAINST). The joint half-level profiles of both teams' corner production and concession rates — rather than full-match averages — determine whether corner totals are front-loaded or back-loaded, a within-match state structure that the full-match average obscures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires within-match half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously and conditions on a cross-team half-level differential — a within-match state structure. It is not reducible to a single team's corner average with one coarse band; it requires the joint half-split profiles of both sides.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-versus-long-run drift for both teams simultaneously: measure the gap between RECENT_5 and ALL_PRIOR for yellow_cards AGAINST Team B, and the gap between RECENT_5 and ALL_PRIOR for yellow_cards FOR Team A. When both gaps move in opposite directions (Team B attracting more cards against, Team A committing fewer), test whether total match yellow cards and the distribution between teams differs from the baseline expectation set by long-run averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent yellow-cards-against rate has risen above its long-run rate while Team A's recent yellow-cards-for rate has fallen below its long-run rate, the disciplinary asymmetry (more cards on Team B's side) is amplified relative to what long-run averages predict; total yellow cards in the match are associated with this joint drift pattern.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card rate against it has spiked sharply in recent matches (AGAINST RECENT_5: 3.6 vs ALL_PRIOR: 1.955), while Team A's yellow card rate FOR has declined (FOR RECENT_5: 0.6 vs ALL_PRIOR: 0.8). This divergence in recent-versus-long-run trajectories for yellow cards on opposing sides — Team B attracting more cards against it recently while Team A is committing fewer fouls recently — represents a regime shift in the disciplinary asymmetry between the two teams that is not captured by either team's long-run average alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-team, two-direction regime-drift mechanism: it requires simultaneously conditioning on the recent-vs-long-run trajectory of yellow cards for both teams in opposite directions. It is not reducible to one team's recent level versus its long-run level (which is already covered); the novelty is the cross-team joint drift in opposing directions as a combined signal.
